thread:
maria: Heads up — GPUs in eu-west-1 edge pool are dropping long-lived gRPC streams to customers. Seeing a bunch of TCP RSTs coming from the edge gateway.
chris: Any deploys or infra changes around the time this started?
maria: No app deploys. CloudTrail shows an automated change to a subnet NACL about ~15m before incidents started — it narrowed the ephemeral port range.
infra-bot: ALERT: NACL acl-0a1b2c3d applied deny 0.0.0.0/0 ports 1024-65535 to subnet-0f1e2d3c at 1865432005 (auto-remediate).
ayn: If the NACL is blocking high ports that will break the return path for ephemeral source ports. gRPC streams use long-lived TCP connections; NAT behavior + stateless NACLs can cause return packets to be dropped and trigger RSTs. Could also be asymmetric routing if NAT SNAT happens in a different AZ.
chris: I grabbed a tcpdump on one of the nodes. snippet:
```
15:42:10.123456 IP client-ip.54321 > node-ip.50051: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535
15:42:10.123480 IP node-ip.50051 > client-ip.54321: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1
15:42:10.123500 IP client-ip.54321 > node-ip.50051: Flags [.], ack 1
... connection works for ~12 minutes ...
15:54:20.654321 IP gw-ip.40000 > node-ip.54321: Flags [R], seq 0
```
chris: Note: RST sourced from gateway IP and a high source port. Looks like return path got rejected and gateway reset connection.
maria: Quick workaround — I explicitly opened 1024-65535 in the NACL for the canary subnets and the gRPC streams recovered. But that's a bandaid. Root cause appears to be the auto-remediate policy that accidentally applied a restrictive NACL to one AZ/subnet during a rollout, plus NAT gateway source-port mapping causing return traffic to traverse that subnet.
ops-lead: @maria can you capture VPC Flow Logs for the affected timeframe and check which eni/gw handled the return path? Also verify route tables and source/dest check on NAT instance if we're using a self-managed NAT. If it's AWS-managed NAT Gateway, check if there's an AZ failover causing asymmetry.
maria: Flow logs show many "REJECT" entries matching the NACL deny on dst ports 1024-65535 from the gw IP. I also found two NACLs attached to the same subnet (one from an older rollout), so attachment order during the automation caused the restrictive one to be active. I'll revert the auto-remediate change and remove the stray NACL attachment.
chris: Can we add a quick CI/alert to detect NACL diffs and make ephemeral port coverage mandatory for edge subnets? Also consider recommending stateful SGs + NLB for customer-facing streams to avoid stateless NACL pitfalls.
maria: Plan: 1) revert NACL change in remaining subnets (in progress) 2) patch auto-remediate rule to exclude edge subnets 3) add alerting for NACL/SG diffs + ephemeral-port checks 4) postmortem + runbook updates. Rolling fixes now, will follow up with postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
